reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Low erythropoietin plus JAK2 means polycythaemia vera; high EPO means secondary
Teardrop dacrocytes plus leukoerythroblastic film plus dry tap mean myelofibrosis
Aquagenic itch and Budd Chiari thrombosis hint polycythaemia vera
reference.pathophysiology: Constitutive JAK STAT signalling from JAK2, CALR or MPL mutations frees stem cell progeny from growth controls, overproducing one or more mature lines until fibrosis, exhaustion or blast transformation supervenes. Dysplastic clones instead accumulate splicing, epigenetic and chromosomal lesions causing maturation arrest with intramedullary apoptosis and leukaemic potential.
additionalDifferentials: Primary versus secondary erythrocytosis by erythropoietin
Myeloproliferative overproduction versus myelodysplastic ineffective production
Myelofibrosis versus metastatic marrow replacement film clues
